title: Define and prove space, layout, and responsive behaviour
objective: Create a canonical spatial system for Mez that turns approved typography and colour into repeatable content widths, grids, gutters, section rhythm, density modes, and responsive behaviour from 320px through wide desktop.

included: spacing primitives and semantic spacing roles
content widths, grid, gutter, section rhythm, and density contracts
breakpoints and responsive recomposition rules from 320px through wide desktop
realistic marketing, commerce, document, email, and dense-interface layout fixtures
overflow, copy expansion, alignment, equal-geometry, and intentional-break fixtures
generated tokens, schema, guidance, and a bounded human spatial-character proof
excluded: changing canonical typography or colour values
final radius, border, shadow, elevation, or control implementation

acceptance: one semantic source generates spatial tokens and responsive contracts
content-width, grid, gutter, rhythm, and density rules are mechanically verifiable
canonical typography and colour remain unchanged
realistic fixtures recompose from 320px through wide desktop
equal geometry and intentional alignment breaks are explicit
human verdict can be recorded without changing unrelated foundations

verification.passCondition: source, generated tokens, responsive contracts, and task records validate
320, 375, 430, 768, 1024, 1280, and 1440 fixtures preserve reading order and avoid two-dimensional overflow
copy expansion, dense content, sparse content, zoom, and alignment stress fixtures satisfy the declared contract
Olli approves the spatial rhythm and responsive character

humanGate.approvalQuestion: Does this spacing, grid, rhythm, density, and responsive system feel recognisably Mez while remaining useful from 320px through wide desktop?

stopConditions: a spatial rule requires changing canonical typography or colour values
a required viewport needs horizontal page scrolling or loses content order
equal geometry and intentional alignment breaks cannot be expressed as explicit rules
the proof combines control-finish, product-expression, or homepage decisions with the spatial gate
notes: Begin with a read-only audit of existing spatial evidence and token conflicts before implementation.
FND-01 typography and FND-02 colour are canonical inputs, not design variables for this task.
FND-04 retains authority over final geometry, border, depth, and controls.
